chunks: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Walid al-Salmy narrated to us, saying: Abulfazl Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Katib al-Neishaboory narrated through his chain, raising it to the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him),

that he said to his sons: 'O my sons! Beware of animosity with men, for they are not free from two types: a wise one who plots against you, or an ignorant one who hastens to retaliate against you. Speech is male and response is female; when the two mates come together, there must be offspring.' Then he began to recite: 'Safe from injury is he who avoids the reply, And he who flatters men has succeeded. He who fears men, they will fear him, And he who despises men, they will not fear him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the metaphor of male speech and female response in Imam Ali's advice to his children?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) provides a pragmatic sociological analysis of human interaction, warning that one must guard against both the calculated cunning of the wise and the impulsive aggression of the ignorant. The metaphor of speech as male and response as female underscores the inevitability of consequences arising from the union of action and reaction, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on social prudence (*hilm*). This advice reflects the Imam’s broader strategy of navigating political and social turbulence through calculated restraint and awareness of human nature.
